article.description: — Aaliyah Edwards scored a career-high 26 points to go with 10 rebounds, and Diamond Miller added 21 points as the Connecticut Sun beat the Chicago Sky 87-81 on Tuesday night.

article.story: UNCASVILLE, Conn. -- — Aaliyah Edwards scored a career-high 26 points to go with 10 rebounds, and Diamond Miller added 21 points as the Connecticut Sun beat the Chicago Sky 87-81 on Tuesday night. Connecticut had a 78-58 lead — its largest of the game — early in the fourth quarter before Chicago clawed within 82-79 with 2:20 left following a 21-4 run. The Sun scored the next four points, highlighted by Edwards' block and layup for a seven-point lead. Kennedy Burke added 19 points for Connecticut (10-27). Edwards was 11 of 16 from the field in 26 minutes and topped her previous best of 24 points. Brittney Griner (left knee) and Olivia Nelson-Ododa (right knee) did not play. Kamilla Cardoso led Chicago (15-24) with 24 points and 13 rebounds for her 14th double-double this season. Azura Stevens added 18 points. Courtney Vandersloot became the second player in WNBA history to reach 3,000 career assists, doing so with the highest average per game. Connecticut led 44-29 at halftime after holding the Sky to 33% shooting, including 0 of 12 from 3-point range. Sun starters Edwards (15 points), Burke (11) and Miller (10) combined to outscore Chicago 36-29 in the first half. Chicago was without two of its guards in the second half due to injuries. Starter Natasha Cloud (right knee injury) played 16 minutes in the first half and DiJonai Carrington (foot) logged four minutes. Up next Sky: At New York on Saturday. Sun: Host Golden State on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here

articles.headline: How Bueckers, Clark, Reese will impact Team USA at World Cup
articles.description: The future is here for Team USA as Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and others make their debut in a major event.

images.name: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese [1296x729]
images.caption: Angel Reese, left, and Caitlin Clark are among seven Team USA players making their senior national team debut at a major 5-on-5 event.

images.name: USA Basketball youth movement [1296x729]
images.caption: From left to right, Sonia Citron, Angel Reese, Kiki Iriafen, Paige Bueckers and Caitlin Clark were each drafted into the WNBA since April 2024.

images.name: Aliyah Boston and Angel Reese [1296x729]
images.caption: With reigning World Cup and Olympic MVP A'ja Wilson sidelined by injury, Aliyah Boston and Angel Reese will undoubtedly have  more responsibility in Team USA's frontcourt.

articles.headline: Wings' Li to miss FIBA World Cup due to lost passport
articles.description: China will have to play without Li Yueru at the women's FIBA World Cup after her replacement passport was lost in the mail ahead of the tournament that starts in Germany this week.

images.name: Li Yueru [600x400]
images.caption: Li Yueru has had a series of strong performances since being traded to the Dallas Wings last month.

articles.headline: 2026 WNBA championship odds: Lynx still odds-on title favorites; Aces, Valkyries next
articles.description: The Lynx remain odds-on favorites to win the WNBA championship, while the red-hot Valkyries are back up to third on the oddsboard.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier, Olivia Miles and the Lynx are winners of 16 of their past 17 games.
images.alt: Olivia Miles #5 of the Minnesota Lynx reacts to a foul call next to Napheesa Collier #24 during WNBA game against the Golden State Valkyries on August 19, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, CA.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier and the Lynx enter the week at even money to win the WNBA championship.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx drives to the basket during the game against the Las Vegas Aces on August 15, 2026 at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier, Natasha Howard and the Minnesota Lynx continue to roll.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx celebrates with teammate Natasha Howard #1 against the Toronto Tempo during the second half at Scotiabank Arena on July 30, 2026 in Toronto, Canada.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier's welcome return only boosts a Lynx team that's the current favorite to win the WNBA Finals.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx shoots a free throw during the game against the Seattle Storm on July 22, 2026 at Climate Pledge Arena in Seattle, Washington.

images.name: Olivia Miles for Odds File (260720) [1296x729]
images.caption: Rookie of the Year front-runner Olivia Miles is one of the big reasons that the sportsbooks have made the Minnesota Lynx the team to beat for the championship this season.
images.alt: Olivia Miles #5 of the Minnesota Lynx looks on during the game against the Portland Fire on July 18, 2026 at Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

images.name: Gabby Williams  [1296x729]
images.caption: Gabby Williams leads the Valkyries in scoring with 15.0 PPG.
images.alt: Gabby Williams #1 of the Golden State Valkyries dribbles the ball during the game =a  on July 6, 2026 at  CareFirst Arena in Washington, D.C.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Olivia Miles and the Minnesota Lynx are now alone in front as favorites to win the WNBA championship.
images.alt: Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles (5) dribbles past Dallas Wings guard Azzi Fudd (35) during the WNBA game between the Dallas Wings and the Minnesota Lynx on June 28, 2026, at College Park Center in Arlington, TX.

images.name: Natasha Howard of Minnesota Lynx [608x342]
images.caption: A strong start to the season has the Lynx tied with the Aces for the shortest title odds, just ahead of the Liberty.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: The Lynx have seen their odds shorten but have a tough schedule this week.
images.alt: Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles (5) drives past Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers during the second half of a WNBA basketball game in Arlington, Texas, Thursday, May 14, 2026.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Rookie of the Year favorite Olivia Miles is helping drive the early success of the Minnesota Lynx.

images.name: Paige Bueckers [1296x729]
images.caption: Paige Bueckers and her 19.3 PPG is a big reason for the encouraging start by the Wings.
images.alt: Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers (5) drives to the basket against Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud (9) during the second half at Wintrust Arena.

images.name: A'ja Wilson [1296x729]
images.caption: The Las Vegas Aces, led by reigning MVP A'ja Wilson, are again one of the favorites to win the WNBA championship this season.
images.alt: Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson (22) celebrates a play with teammates during the first half of a WNBA preseason basketball game against the Dallas Wings in Austin, Texas, Sunday, May 3, 2026.

images.name: Satou Sabally [1296x729]
images.caption: The New York Liberty made some free agent moves, most notably signing Satou Sabally.

images.name: Angel Reese [1296x729]
images.caption: Angel Reese heads to Atlanta after two seasons in Chicago.
images.alt: Chicago Sky forward Angel Reese (5) dribbles against the Atlanta Dream in the first quarter at Gateway Center Arena at College Park.

articles.headline: U.S. coach Kara Lawson calls World Cup most challenging
articles.description: U.S. coach Kara Lawson says this version of the FIBA World Cup is the most challenging she's seen.

articles.headline: Sky's Skylar Diggins (knee) to miss remainder of season
articles.description: Chicago Sky guard Skylar Diggins will miss the remainder of the WNBA's season as she continues to recover from a right knee injury, the team announced Tuesday.
